title: A goal whose money was moved to its own account is counted at that account; the account it left gets no warning for it (decision V1)
story: Set up Mon 4 Jan 2027: the bank holds 150,000 (minimum 20,000), of which Trip 50,000, Food 40,000 and Free to spend 60,000 (typed, its opening split); a savings account opens the same day at 0. Pay of 300,000 on the 25th (moved earlier). On Wed 6 Jan the person moves Trip's money to its own account: 50,000 goes from the bank to Savings, and Trip is now kept in Savings (its own account). The file is the copy after the move: Trip's kept_in is Savings, mode own_account; the opening split stays where it was typed, on the bank. Every amount is made up.

events.note: Trip's money moved to its own account

asks.question: bank_today
asks.why: 150,000 (opening) - 50,000 (Trip's money moved to Savings, Wed 6 Jan) = 100,000

asks.question: place
asks.why: 50,000 (Trip's opening split, typed on the bank; the move took the money, not the place's balance) = 50,000
asks.note: Before V1 the model looked for Trip's split only on the account it is kept in now: 0.

asks.question: safe_to_spend
asks.note: Before V1: 50,000, Trip's money counted as free on Savings.

asks.question: safe_to_spend
asks.note: Trip is no longer held on the bank; held there it would show 10,000 below the minimum (the false warning of final_review_3).

asks.question: warnings
asks.why: The bank keeps 40,000 above its minimum; Savings holds exactly Trip; nothing is below its minimum.

asks.question: headline
asks.why: 40,000 (the bank's safe to spend, below Free to spend's 60,000 this period, so it holds the headline; Savings has nothing free) = 40,000
asks.note: Before V1: 60,000, Savings' 50,000 counted as free.
